raw_case_text: A 26-year-old male presented with documented fever, anorexia with mild nausea for 20 days. Fever work-ups including malarial antigen test, dengue, typhus, Widal test, and urine routine microscopy were done outside, and all were negative. At admission, vitals were stable, hemogram revealed a leucocyte count of 6700/muL, with normal hemoglobin and platelets. Elevated value of ESR was 68/hr and CRP (18 mg/dL). Chest X-ray was normal. Ultrasound abdomen showed minimum free fluid in the abdomen, ileal thickening for a segment 6 cm of size 9 mm, with few mesenteric lymph nodes. Computed tomography abdomen confirmed the ultrasound findings (Fig. 4). Blood culture revealed S. typhi growth on the third day of admission. Ceftriaxone was given but the fever didn't respond by the 7th day when the patient underwent colonoscopy. Meanwhile, the IGRA test was positive and tuberculosis suspicion arose. On colonoscopy, ascending colon and caecum showed few superficial ulcers maximum size 5-6 mm with surrounding erythema seen. The ileocecal valve and ileum to 12 cm displayed edematous mucosa with superficial ulcers, ileum was less distensible. Beyond 12 cm transition to normal mucosa is seen. Ileum is seen till 30 cm. A few more superficial ulcers maximum 8 mm in size were seen around 20 cm while the rest of the mucosa was normal (Fig. 5). Biopsy from ileocecum showed preserved architecture with marked surface ulceration with dense and diffuse lymphohistiocytic admixed with neutrophilic inflammatory infiltrate. No acid-fast bacilli or fungal organisms were identified on special stains. Gene Xpert test was negative. Fever responded to the 12th day of antibiotics and the course was given for five more days. At the 6-month follow-up review CT scan showed normal ileum and no lymphadenopathy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old male presented with documented fever, anorexia, and mild nausea for 20 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced documented fevers, anorexia, and mild nausea for 20 days. Outpatient workup performed prior to admission—including malarial antigen test, dengue serology, typhus serology, febrile agglutination serology, and routine urinalysis—was entirely negative. Persistent symptoms prompted hospital admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for anorexia and mild nausea. Denies other systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Vitals were documented as stable on admission. Systemic examination findings were not detailed.
objective.routine_investigations: Leucocyte count 6700/muL, normal hemoglobin and platelets, ESR 68 mm/hr, and C-reactive protein 18 mg/dL. Chest X-ray was normal. Routine urine microscopy was normal. Malarial antigen test, dengue testing, typhus testing, and febrile agglutinins were negative. Abdominal ultrasound showed minimal free fluid in the abdomen, ileal thickening over a 6 cm segment measuring 9 mm in wall thickness, and a few mesenteric lymph nodes.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT confirmed ultrasound findings of minimal peritoneal free fluid, 6 cm segment of ileal thickening measuring 9 mm, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy. Interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) was positive. Colonoscopy revealed a few superficial ulcers measuring up to 5-6 mm with surrounding erythema in the ascending colon and caecum; the ileocecal valve and ileum up to 12 cm displayed edematous mucosa with superficial ulcers and reduced distensibility, with normal mucosa beyond 12 cm and a few additional superficial ulcers (up to 8 mm) at 20 cm. Biopsy from the ileocecum demonstrated preserved architecture with marked surface ulceration and dense, diffuse lymphohistiocytic and neutrophilic inflammatory infiltrate; special stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungal organisms were negative, and GeneXpert was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Salmonella typhi bacteremia (typhoid fever) confirmed by blood culture yielding S. typhi growth on the third day of hospitalization. Despite a positive IGRA, active intestinal tuberculosis was ruled out based on negative AFB stains, negative fungal stains, negative GeneXpert, and biopsy histology; malaria, dengue, and typhus were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone. Fever persisted through day 7, with defervescence finally achieved on day 12 of antibiotic therapy. Ceftriaxone was continued for 5 additional days. At 6-month follow-up, repeat abdominal CT demonstrated complete normalization of the ileum and complete resolution of lymphadenopathy.
